HomeEssentials Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jennifer Hayes, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Hayes, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer; Karen Lee, Chief Stores Officer; and Brian Walsh, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the Q2 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We achieved comparable store sales growth of 4.2% year-over-year, our third straight quarter of positive comps and accelerating from Q1's 2.8%, outperforming peers amid stabilizing traffic and strong category execution in hardlines and garden categories.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital sales surged 32% year-over-year to $450 million, now representing 22% of total net sales, driven by our mobile app enhancements, ship-from-store expansion, and BOPIS surge, fueling omnichannel synergy.

3. Store Performance: Our remodel program is delivering, with 85 completions so far this year on track for 220, yielding 6-8% comp lifts and quick paybacks, as we transform stores into experiential hubs.

4. Marketing Initiatives: Digital marketing effectiveness shone with 6.2x ROAS, up significantly, powering store traffic and conversions through AI personalization and geofencing, while ad expenses trended up but with improving efficiency.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: We realized efficiencies from nearshoring, stabilized freight costs, and inventory discipline at 13 weeks, supporting gross margin gains and resilience against disruptions.

6. Loyalty Program Update: Our HomeEssentials Rewards program hit 65 million active members, up 8%, driving frequency and basket stability, contributing to 42% of comp sales.

7. Sustainability Initiatives: Remodels target LEED Silver with LED retrofits, solar canopies, and EV charging, cutting energy use 30% and attracting eco-conscious shoppers.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Rachel Kim to provide more details on our financial results.

Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $3.1 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year, reflecting strong comps and digital acceleration. Gross margin was 39.0%, primarily driven by supply chain efficiencies, private label growth, and disciplined promotions. Operating expenses were $860 million, representing 27.7% of revenue, with leverage from productivity gains. Net income was $245 million, or $0.76 per share. We generated $380 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently at 13.5 weeks of supply, down from 14 weeks and on track to 12.5 weeks by year-end, minimizing markdown risk.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

To give more color on some of these highlights Alex mentioned, let me start with our comparable store sales performance. As Alex noted, comp store sales grew 4.2% year-over-year in Q2, marking our third consecutive quarter of positive comps and accelerating from 2.8% in Q1. This beat our guidance of 2% to 3.5% and topped the retail sector average, where companies like Macy's were flat and Kohl's at just 1.1%. Traffic rose 1.5% year-over-year, supported by our Storefront Revival initiative with experiential zones in 450 locations, lifting dwell time 12% in tests. Average unit retail increased 2.6%, thanks to a shift to higher-margin big-ticket items like appliances and outdoor sets up 8.2%. Conversion stayed at 28.5%, but private-label Essentials Elite, now 22% of sales, grew 15% on comps.

By category, hardlines led with 6.1% comps from DIY demand and DeWalt partnerships. Softlines were 1.2%, garden and outdoor exploded at 9.4%, seasonal decor up 3.7%, and wellness/home office flat but stable with RFID reducing stockouts 22%. Regionally, Southeast and Southwest hit 7.3% on migration trends in Florida and Texas, Midwest 2.4%, Northeast -0.8% addressed by urban remodels. BOPIS drove 18% of store sales, loyalty 42%, and we're guiding Q3 comps to 3.5-5.0% and full-year to 4.0%.

Next, on e-commerce growth, which Alex highlighted. E-commerce sales rose 32% year-over-year to $450 million in Q2, accelerating from 25% in Q1 and outpacing the industry's 15-18%. This brings digital to 22% of total net sales, up from 15%, with GMV up 35% to $520 million on $145 AOV, up 12%. Our app handled 62% of orders, AI recommendations boosting conversions 28% to 4.2%. Ship-from-store covers 95% of U.S. stores for same-day delivery in metros, BOPIS up 45% to $120 million, adding store impulse buys. U.S. up 35%, Canada 28%, Europe 22%, with Asia pilot at 55%. Apparel led at 40%, home 30%, electronics 25%. CAC steady at $18, LTV to $450. We expect 25-30% H2 growth.

Before handing over, I want to cover our full-year fiscal 2025 guidance and key assumptions, as well as Q1 FY25 outlook. For FY25, consolidated revenue $12.8-13.1 billion, 2-5% growth; comps 1.5-3.5%; digital 12-15% growth to 28-30% of sales; gross margin 38.5-39.5%, up 50-100 bps; adjusted op income $950M-$1.05B; EBITDA margin 10.5-11%; EPS $2.85-$3.15.

Key assumptions include U.S. GDP 2-2.5%, PCE 2.2%, CPI 2.5-3%; 1-2% traffic growth; remodels contributing 40-60 bps to comps; input costs stable, private label 42% driving 150 bps margin; inventory to 12.5 weeks; SG&A 28-28.5%; regional variance with Sunbelt strong. Upside from omnichannel, risks from GDP miss or tariffs. Conservatively buffered.

For Q1 FY25, sales $2.55-2.65B flat to +2%; comps 1-2%; gross margin 36.5-37.0%; SG&A 24-24.5%; op income $320-350M; EPS $0.85-0.95. Full-year sales $10.7-11.0B, comps 2.5-3.5%, gross margin up 75-125 bps to 37.2-37.7%, op income $1.25-1.35B, EPS $3.60-3.80.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Tom Rivera, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Karen Lee to discuss store operations, and then Brian Walsh to discuss marketing initiatives.

Tom Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Rachel. This quarter, we launched our expanded Essentials Home private label line, which has seen strong uptake with double-digit growth in velocity and 55% gross margins, outperforming national brands by 2x in repeat purchases. We're excited about the potential of this and other upcoming launches like sustainable kitchenware at 20-30% below competitors.

Karen Lee, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Tom. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. Let me dive deeper into our remodel and renovation plans, a cornerstone of our strategy with 1,250 locations. We're allocating $357 million of $650 million capex to 220 remodels, 15 relocations, and five small-format stores. Pilots showed 6.2-8.4% comp lifts, AUV to $1,250/sq ft, payback 24 months, EBITDA +150 bps.

The Store 2.0 template at $1.6M per store features layout optimization with experiential zones boosting basket 15%, RFID for 98% accuracy, BOPIS lockers, AI kiosks upselling 18%, LEED Silver with 30% energy savings, solar, EV charging, labor productivity +12%. Lab stores test AR mirrors for 10-15% conversions. Northeast premium focus 9% lifts, Southeast value 7% traffic, West sustainability. FY25 250 remodels position us for mid-single-digit comps and 200 bps EBITDA expansion to 12.5%.

Brian Walsh, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Karen. Our marketing efforts are fueling traffic. First, on expense trends: Q2 marketing and advertising hit $45.2 million, up 18.4% YoY to 2.8% of sales, but ROAS improved to 4.8x from 4.2x. Digital now 55% of spend, programmatic CTV up BOPIS 22%; AI personalization via Salesforce CDP cut CAC 12% to $28; geofencing 3.2x ROAS; Southeast up 25% driving 14% comps. Q3 mid-teens growth to 2.7-2.9%, targeting 5.5x ROAS.

On digital effectiveness specifically: Spend $45 million, ROAS 6.2x ahead of peers, attributing $279 million revenue, 28% of store sales. Paid search 42% spend, CPC down to $1.44, 2.5M store visits; social 4.1x with first-party data; display 3.8x geofencing; email/SMS 12.4x recovering $18M. North America 6.5x, Europe 4.9x. Tech like GA4 server-side, Einstein AI cut CAC 14%; digital flywheel grew visits 8% YoY.

Our new Home Refresh campaign has increased brand awareness by 25%.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Chris Anderson with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Chris Anderson (Bank of America):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of persistent inflation on your sales?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Chris. Inflation at 3.4% in Q2 pressured big-ticket items like our Signature Series furniture, where we modeled just 1% growth versus 5% in consumables. But our outlook assumes CPI moderating to 2.5-3%, supporting discretionary home goods, especially kitchen/bath up 4% YTD. Our essentials mix and loyalty insights into $75K-150K households show stable baskets at $85 with 3% frequency uptick, insulating us better than peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Simmons with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Laura Simmons (Wells Fargo):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Laura. For Q3, we're guiding comps to 3.5% to 5.0%, building on Q2 momentum with traffic tailwinds from remodels, moderating inflation freeing wallet share, and omnichannel lifts. Full-year now at 4.0%, assuming stable gas prices and weather-neutral conditions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline (Citigroup):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Robert. We've nearshored 20% of Mexico SKUs, stabilizing ocean freight at $3,500/FEU from 2022 peaks, locked fixed-price contracts, and ramped private label to 42% with RFID for 98% accuracy in remodels. Shrink down, stockouts reduced 30% via ML forecasting, mirroring Walmart—positioning us for 50-100 bps gross margin expansion despite risks like Red Sea or tariffs on 15% China imports.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Patel with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Dana Patel (Deutsche Bank):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great to hear, Dana. HomeEssentials Rewards with 65 million actives, up 8%, drives 42% of comps—basket stable, frequency up 3% in core demo. It fuels personalization like SmartCart AI for 150 bps margins, 25% of sales via app/beacons, boosting CLV 11% and tying digital to stores seamlessly.

Operator:
Thank you.

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Jennifer Hayes, Vice President of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
